subject: Society and Culture
name: Society and Culture, Year 11
about: HSC, Social worlds, identity and communication
syllabus: NSW Society and Culture Stage 6 Syllabus (2013), Preliminary (Year 11) course

points.title: Society and culture
points.brief: A society is a group of people who share a territory and institutions. Culture is the shared values, beliefs, customs and ways of life they pass on.

points.title: Persons and environment
points.brief: A person is an individual with a unique identity. The environment is the natural and built world people live in and are shaped by.

points.title: Time, continuity and change
points.brief: Some parts of a society stay the same over time while others change, and studying both helps explain the present.

points.title: Power and authority
points.brief: Power is the ability to influence others. Authority is power accepted as legitimate, such as a parent's or a government's.

points.title: Gender and identity
points.brief: Gender is the social roles and expectations attached to being a man, a woman or another identity. Identity is a person's sense of who they are.

points.title: Globalisation and technologies
points.brief: Globalisation links societies through trade, media and travel. Technologies change how people live, work and communicate.

points.title: Primary and secondary research
points.brief: Primary research collects new information first-hand. Secondary research uses information others have already gathered.

points.title: Qualitative and quantitative research
points.brief: Qualitative research explores meanings and experiences in words. Quantitative research measures and counts, giving numbers to analyse.

points.title: Research methods
points.brief: Interviews, questionnaires, focus groups, observation, participant observation, content analysis, case studies and statistical analysis each suit different questions.

points.title: Ethical research
points.brief: Researchers must get informed consent, keep information confidential, avoid harm and respect the people they study.

points.title: Reliability, validity and bias
points.brief: Reliable research gives consistent results, valid research measures what it claims to, and researchers must watch for bias in themselves and their methods.

points.title: Micro, meso and macro levels
points.brief: Society can be studied at the micro level of individuals and families, the meso level of groups and communities, and the macro level of whole nations and the world.

points.title: Socialisation
points.brief: The lifelong process of learning the norms and values of a society, which shapes how people think and act.

points.title: Agents of socialisation
points.brief: Family, peers, school, media and religion each teach people how to behave and what to value.

points.title: Norms, values and roles
points.brief: Norms are expected behaviours, values are what a group thinks is important, and roles are the behaviour expected of a position, such as student or parent.

points.title: Status
points.brief: Ascribed status is given at birth, such as age or family background. Achieved status is earned, such as a job or qualification.

points.title: Self-concept
points.brief: How a person sees themselves, built from their own experiences and from how others treat them.

points.title: Coming of age
points.brief: The move from childhood to adulthood, which different cultures mark at different ages and in different ways.

points.title: Rites of passage
points.brief: Ceremonies that mark a change in status, such as a bar or bat mitzvah, a graduation or a wedding.

points.title: Gender roles and identity
points.brief: Societies teach expectations about how people of each gender should behave, and these expectations change over time and between cultures.

points.title: Autonomy and interdependence
points.brief: As young people grow, they gain autonomy, the ability to make their own choices, while still depending on others.

points.title: Verbal and non-verbal communication
points.brief: People communicate through words and through gestures, eye contact, personal space and tone, all of which differ between cultures.

points.title: Language and culture
points.brief: A language carries a culture's ideas and values, and some words cannot be translated directly.

points.title: Ethnocentrism and cultural relativism
points.brief: Ethnocentrism judges other cultures by the standards of your own. Cultural relativism tries to understand a culture on its own terms.

points.title: Stereotypes and prejudice
points.brief: A stereotype is an oversimplified idea about a group, and prejudice is a judgement made without knowing the person. Both can lead to unfair treatment.

points.title: Culture shock
points.brief: The confusion and stress people can feel in an unfamiliar culture, which usually eases as they adjust.

points.title: Communicating across cultures
points.brief: Listening, asking questions and learning about other cultures help people communicate respectfully in a globalised world.
